findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data if the underlying storage or backups are compromised.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricting public access, so the bucket could default to being accessible more broadly than intended, and there is no explicit block preventing public ACLs/policies.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) without any server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so nothing in this configuration explicitly blocks public ACLs or policies from being applied later, despite it holding sensitive ledger data.
This bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket to prevent public ACLs or policies despite storing proprietary model artifacts.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving operational runbook data (which may include sensitive internal procedures or credentials references) unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public access for this bucket.

The bucket uses the 'log-delivery-write' canned ACL without a corresponding bucket policy or public access block restricting who can write/read logs, which can allow overly broad write access to audit log data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined to prevent public exposure of audit trail logs, which are sensitive from a security-monitoring perspective.
The object is uploaded to a bucket lacking default encryption and does not specify server_side_encryption itself, meaning this potentially sensitive vendor roster file is stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: force_destroy enabled on bucket with data
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without protection, increasing risk of accidental or malicious irreversible data loss for report data.
